plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 1.6.4
plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the geometric inequality used to prove that lim_{x->0} sin x / x = 1 via the Squeezing Theorem. On the left, the unit circle is drawn with three labeled points: (1, 0) on the x-axis, (cos x, sin x) on the circle, and (1, tan x) on the vertical tangent at x = 1, with angle x at the origin and the base labeled 1. On the right, three geometric shapes compare areas side-by-side: a large right triangle with height tan x (area tan x / 2), a circular sector of angle x (area x / 2), and a small right triangle with height sin x (area sin x / 2), with the inequalities Area of triangle >= Area of sector >= Area of triangle written below. The figure establishes the sandwiching inequality tan x / 2 >= x / 2 >= sin x / 2 that, after dividing by sin x / 2, yields cos x <= sin x / x <= 1 / cos x, enabling the Squeezing Theorem to conclude the limit equals 1.

interactionPlan.concept: For 0 < x < π/2, the areas sin x/2 ≤ x/2 ≤ tan x/2 sandwich the circular sector between two triangles, which forces sin x / x → 1 as x → 0.
elements: Left panel: coordinate axes with arrowheads (x-axis horizontal, y-axis vertical), origin at center
Left panel: blue unit circle centered at origin
Left panel: red radius from origin to point (cos x, sin x) extended as a ray to (1, tan x)
Left panel: red dot and label '(1, 0)' at the point where circle meets positive x-axis
Left panel: red dot and label '(cos x, sin x)' with leader arrow to the point on the circle
Left panel: red dot and label '(1, tan x)' at the top of the vertical tangent line x = 1
Left panel: dashed red vertical segment from (1,0) up to (1, tan x)
Left panel: dashed red chord from (cos x, sin x) down to (1, 0)
Left panel: blue highlighted arc from (1,0) to (cos x, sin x)
Left panel: small arc arrow at origin labeled 'x' marking the angle
Left panel: curly brace under the segment from origin to (1,0) labeled '1'
Right panel A: large right triangle with base 1 (labeled) and vertical leg labeled 'tan x', pink fill, red outline, dashed blue arc inside, angle arrow labeled 'x'
Right panel B: circular sector of radius 1 and angle x, pink fill, red straight edges, blue curved arc, base labeled '1', angle arrow labeled 'x'

Right panel C: small triangle with base 1, apex at (cos x, sin x), pink fill, red outline, dashed blue arc bulging outside, dashed red vertical segment showing height, brace labeled 'sin x', angle arrow labeled 'x'
Caption row: 'Area of triangle  ≥  Area of sector  ≥  Area of triangle'
Formula row: 'tan x / 2  ≥  x / 2  ≥  sin x / 2'
Derived inequality annotation: 'cos x ≤ sin x / x ≤ 1 / cos x'
Numeric readout of the three area values for the current x

interactions.label: angle x (radians)
interactions.teaches: As x shrinks, the outer triangle, sector, and inner triangle converge in both shape and area, so the bounds on sin x / x close in on 1.

interactions.label: Panel layout
interactions.teaches: Stacking the three regions on one set of axes makes the nesting inner triangle ⊂ sector ⊂ outer triangle literally visible, which is why the areas are ordered.
Clicking a region or its caption isolates one area and its formula, connecting each picture to its algebraic expression tan x/2, x/2, or sin x/2.

interactions.label: Let x → 0
interactions.teaches: Watching x sweep toward zero shows cos x and 1/cos x both collapsing to 1, squeezing sin x / x between them.

demo_steps.title: The unit circle setup
demo_steps.narration: A single angle x produces three key points: (1,0) on the axis, (cos x, sin x) on the circle, and (1, tan x) on the tangent line. Drag the slider to see all three move together.

demo_steps.title: Three regions, three areas
demo_steps.narration: The same angle defines a big triangle of area tan x/2, a sector of area x/2, and a small triangle of area sin x/2. Click any caption to highlight its region and formula.

demo_steps.title: Nesting makes the order obvious
demo_steps.narration: Overlay the three regions: the small triangle sits inside the sector, which sits inside the big triangle. Containment forces sin x/2 ≤ x/2 ≤ tan x/2.

demo_steps.title: Shrinking the angle
demo_steps.narration: Reduce x and the three nested regions become nearly indistinguishable — their areas crowd together.

demo_steps.title: The squeeze
demo_steps.narration: Dividing the inequality by sin x/2 gives cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x. As x → 0 both bounds go to 1, so sin x / x must go to 1.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The sector is literally trapped between two triangles built from the same angle, so its area x/2 is trapped between sin x/2 and tan x/2 — and as the trap tightens, sin x / x has nowhere to go but 1.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two-zone layout. Left zone: black axes with arrowheads, a blue unit circle centered at the origin, radius drawn in red from origin to the circle point, extended to the vertical tangent line at x = 1; the segment from (1,0) up to (1, tan x) and the chord from (cos x, sin x) to (1,0) are dashed red; small dots in red at the three labeled points with serif labels '(1, tan x)', '(cos x, sin x)' (with leader arrow), '(1, 0)'; a small curved arrow at the origin labeled 'x'; a curly brace beneath the unit-length base labeled '1'. Right zone: three shapes in a row, all sharing a base of length 1 on a common baseline, pink/salmon fill with red outlines; leftmost is the tall right triangle with vertical leg labeled 'tan x' and a dashed blue arc cutting inside it; middle is the sector with a solid blue arc as its curved edge; rightmost is the short triangle whose apex is the circle point, with a dashed blue arc bulging just outside the slanted side, a thin dashed red vertical height line, and a brace labeled 'sin x'. Each shape carries a small angle arrow labeled 'x' at its left vertex and '1' under its base. Two caption rows in serif type below: 'Area of triangle ≥ Area of sector ≥ Area of triangle' and the stacked fractions 'tan x/2 ≥ x/2 ≥ sin x/2'. In Overlaid mode the three shapes are drawn concentrically on one origin with graded pink opacity (darkest = smallest triangle) so the containment reads at a glance, and a live readout shows numeric values for tan x/2, x/2, sin x/2 plus the derived chain cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x. Highlighted region on click gets a saturated red stroke and its formula badge enlarges; non-selected regions fade to light gray-pink.

discrepancies: The rendered screenshot shows an entirely EMPTY figure area — no unit circle, no axes, no triangles, no sector, no captions. Only the control panel is visible, so at step 0 the artifact is not a drop-in replacement for the source image.

The submitted code contains two concatenated copies of the figure script: the first copy is truncated mid-statement at `g.rect(16` and is immediately followed by `// @FIGURE_CODE_BEGIN` and a second full copy. This corrupts the first `drawOverlay` function and almost certainly aborts script execution, which explains the blank canvas.

Evidence of the script aborting is visible in the UI itself: `#demoNarration` and `#stepLabel` (between the ◀ / ▶ buttons) are blank, meaning `applyStep(0)` never ran; the live-values readout is likewise empty.

Consequently every source element is missing from the render: the blue unit circle with the highlighted arc, the red radius / tangent / dashed segments, the three labelled points (1,0), (cos x, sin x), (1, tan x), the horizontal brace labelled 1, the three pink regions with 'tan x' and 'sin x' braces, and the 'Area of triangle ≥ Area of sector ≥ Area of triangle' caption row with the tan x/2 ≥ x/2 ≥ sin x/2 fractions.
Interactive controls (angle slider, overlay checkbox, x→0 player, step arrows) are present in the panel but produce no visible change because the drawing layer never initialised.
evaluation.notes: The intended design (unit-circle panel plus three pink regions, captions, nesting overlay, angle slider and x→0 player) is conceptually sound and closely matched to the source, but the delivered code is a duplicated/truncated concatenation that breaks execution: the rendered screenshot shows a completely blank figure with empty narration and step labels, so nothing of the source figure is actually visible.

Guided demo — the squeeze setup

Click any pink region or its caption to isolate one area and its formula.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The 'sin x' brace label on the third panel is clipped at the right edge of the viewBox — only 'sir' is visible in the render (text starts at ~x=1140 with viewBox width 1160).

Two extra numeric readout lines (tan x/2 ≥ x/2 ≥ sin x/2 and cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x) are drawn inside the figure below the formulas; they are not in the source and render as tiny, near-illegible grey/red text.

Overall type scale is too small at inline size: the source's prominent serif captions ('Area of triangle', 'tan x', '(1, tan x)') are rendered at roughly half the visual weight they have in the source because the 1160×430 viewBox is shrunk into a ~600 px column.

Left panel: '(1, tan x)' is placed to the right of the tangent point with a grey leader line rather than directly above it as in the source, and the source's dark maroon base segment/brace grouping is less visually distinct.

The blue arc emphasis differs slightly: in the source the middle sector panel's arc is a thick solid blue while panels 1 and 3 use dashed blue; generated matches, but the dashes are much finer relative to the panel size.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful reproduction of the unit-circle + three-area squeeze figure with an excellent set of meaningful interactions (slider, step demo, overlay nesting, x→0 animation, click-to-isolate), but label legibility is weak at inline size and the 'sin x' brace label is clipped off the right edge.
action_items: Widen the viewBox (or shift CEN[2] left) so the third panel's brace and 'sin x' label fit entirely inside the canvas instead of being clipped at x≈1160.

Increase base font sizes (or reduce viewBox width toward ~900) so captions and point labels remain comfortably readable when the figure is shrunk into a narrow column; keep a clear hierarchy with 'Area of …' captions larger than the numeric readout.
Move the two in-figure numeric readout lines into the side panel only (they already appear there) to remove duplicate, illegible text from the artwork.
Place '(1, tan x)' directly above the tangent dot as in the source and drop the grey leader line when the label already sits adjacent to its point.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound (no failure modes, no plan action items); all issues are concrete rendering fixes — clipped label, font sizing, duplicate readouts, and label placement.

demo_steps.title: Nesting makes the order obvious
demo_steps.narration: Overlay the three regions: the small triangle sits inside the sector, which sits inside the big triangle. Containment forces sin x/2 ≤ x/2 ≤ tan x/2.

demo_steps.title: Shrinking the angle
demo_steps.narration: Reduce x and the three nested regions become nearly indistinguishable — their areas crowd together.

demo_steps.title: The squeeze
demo_steps.narration: Dividing the inequality by sin x/2 gives cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x. As x → 0 both bounds go to 1, so sin x / x must go to 1.

plan.keyInsight: The sector is literally trapped between two triangles built from the same angle, so its area x/2 is trapped between sin x/2 and tan x/2 — and as the trap tightens, sin x / x has nowhere to go but 1.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Two-zone layout. Left zone: black axes with arrowheads, a blue unit circle centered at the origin, radius drawn in red from origin to the circle point, extended to the vertical tangent line at x = 1; the segment from (1,0) up to (1, tan x) and the chord from (cos x, sin x) to (1,0) are dashed red; small dots in red at the three labeled points with serif labels '(1, tan x)', '(cos x, sin x)' (with leader arrow), '(1, 0)'; a small curved arrow at the origin labeled 'x'; a curly brace beneath the unit-length base labeled '1'. Right zone: three shapes in a row, all sharing a base of length 1 on a common baseline, pink/salmon fill with red outlines; leftmost is the tall right triangle with vertical leg labeled 'tan x' and a dashed blue arc cutting inside it; middle is the sector with a solid blue arc as its curved edge; rightmost is the short triangle whose apex is the circle point, with a dashed blue arc bulging just outside the slanted side, a thin dashed red vertical height line, and a brace labeled 'sin x'. Each shape carries a small angle arrow labeled 'x' at its left vertex and '1' under its base. Two caption rows in serif type below: 'Area of triangle ≥ Area of sector ≥ Area of triangle' and the stacked fractions 'tan x/2 ≥ x/2 ≥ sin x/2'. In Overlaid mode the three shapes are drawn concentrically on one origin with graded pink opacity (darkest = smallest triangle) so the containment reads at a glance, and a live readout shows numeric values for tan x/2, x/2, sin x/2 plus the derived chain cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x. Highlighted region on click gets a saturated red stroke and its formula badge enlarges; non-selected regions fade to light gray-pink.

discrepancies: Label sizing/placement in the left panel differs: '(1, 0)' sits above-right of the point rather than to the right at axis level, and the three point labels render at roughly 10–11 px at inline size, noticeably smaller and more crowded than the prominent serif annotations in the source.

The generated figure adds a red italic line 'cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x' beneath the fraction row, plus a numeric readout panel, which do not exist in the source (pedagogically reasonable but an addition).

In the source the tangent segment and the chord to (1,0) are dashed red while the ray from the origin is solid; the generated version matches this, but the dark radius segment along the x-axis is thinner/less visible than the source's heavy dark unit segment.

The source's small arrow/leader for '(cos x, sin x)' points at the circle point from the right; in the generated version the leader is short and the label block sits close to '(1, 0)', creating mild crowding in the upper-right of the circle panel.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-composed reproduction of the unit-circle/sector/triangle squeeze figure with genuinely useful interactions (angle slider, nesting overlay, x→0 animation, click-to-isolate regions, 5-step demo); main weaknesses are slightly undersized and mildly crowded annotation labels in the left panel and a few non-source additions below the formula row.
action_items: Increase point-label font size in the left circle panel (e.g. 19–20 in viewbox units) and reposition '(1, 0)' to the right of the dot at axis level as in the source, adding a small offset so it no longer crowds '(cos x, sin x)'.
Thicken/darken the unit radius segment along the x-axis and shorten the '(cos x, sin x)' leader arrow so it clearly terminates at the circle point, matching the source's leader style.

Move the added 'cos x ≤ sin x/x ≤ 1/cos x' line into the side panel readout (or render it larger and visually separated) so the default step-0 view is a closer drop-in replacement for the static source.
Scale the whole viewbox slightly larger (or reduce VH) so the figure fills more of the container width/height and all caption text renders comfortably at inline size.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are sound (no failure modes, concept 5/5); remaining issues are concrete rendering fixes—label sizing/placement, stroke weight, leader length, and viewbox scaling—which belong to the generator.
